title: Ten minutes — pack the carpet-bag
learning_goal: Know what went into the carpet-bag and what stayed at Savile Row; feel the scramble.

narration.script: Twenty-five past seven. Fogg comes home from the club. He calls Passepartout and says: 'We start for Dover and Calais in ten minutes.' Dover is on the English coast; Calais is across the sea, in France. Where to? 'We are going round the world.' 'In eighty days.' Passepartout, remember, wanted a quiet life. Now help him pack. One carpet-bag — one travel bag — must hold everything. Drag in what goes; leave what stays. Two shirts and three pairs of stockings each. A mackintosh and a travelling-cloak. The red-bound Bradshaw — a thick book of train times, hundreds of pages. And a fat roll of Bank of England notes: twenty thousand pounds. No books — the house has none. The electric clock stays on the mantel. And so, tonight, does the gas — remember that. Two shirts, three pairs of stockings, and half a fortune.
